To: All Production Staff, Line 3
From: Greta Lindqvist, Plant Operations Manager
Date: March 4
Subject: Scheduled maintenance shutdown

Please be advised that Line 3 will be shut down for scheduled maintenance from Monday, March 11, through Wednesday, March 13. During this period, our contracted technicians from Halverson Industrial Services will replace the conveyor belt motors and recalibrate the packaging sensors, which have caused several slowdowns over the past quarter.

All Line 3 operators will be temporarily reassigned to Line 5, where we are increasing output to meet a large order from Dexfield Appliances. Your shift supervisors will distribute updated schedules by Friday, March 8. Note that the morning shift on Line 5 will begin thirty minutes earlier than usual, at 6:30 A.M., for the duration of the reassignment.

Employees who have completed forklift certification are asked to contact me directly, as we need two additional certified drivers in the loading area during the shutdown. Overtime pay will apply to any hours worked beyond your regular schedule.

Thank you for your flexibility as we complete these necessary upgrades.

Yuna Choi

To: All Warehouse Staff, Norvale Distribution Center
From: Tomasz Krupa, Inventory Control Manager

Subject: New cycle counting procedure

Starting February 1, the Norvale Distribution Center will replace its annual full-facility inventory count with a cycle counting program. Instead of closing the warehouse for two days each December, small sections of inventory will be counted continuously throughout the year.

Under the new system, each aisle will be counted at least once per quarter. High-value items, such as electronics stored in the secured cage, will be counted monthly. Counts will take place during the first hour of the morning shift, before order picking begins, to minimize disruption.

A team of six staff members will be designated as cycle counters on a rotating basis. Counters will use the handheld scanners already in use for receiving; a software update enabling the counting module will be installed on January 25. A mandatory forty-five-minute orientation will be held in the break room on January 28 at 8:00 A.M. and repeated at 2:30 P.M. for the afternoon shift.

Carmody Savings Bank Launches Mobile Banking App for Small Businesses

LERWICK (October 22) — Carmody Savings Bank today released Carmody Biz, a mobile application created specifically for the bank's small-business customers. "We reversed that approach and designed every screen around how a business actually operates."

One feature that emerged directly from the panel's feedback is the app's invoice tool, which lets users create and send invoices and then matches incoming payments to them automatically. Panel member Dario Fuentes, who owns a landscaping company in Lerwick, said the feature has already saved him several hours of bookkeeping each week.

Larkspur will publish a progress report every six months on its website, where customers can also find instructions for composting the plant-based film at home. The company joins a growing list of apparel brands, including Tornquist & Co. and Fellbright, that have made similar pledges in the past two years.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Pagewell Books Marks 40th Anniversary with Expansion into Three Cities

ROSSDALE (August 5) — Pagewell Books, the independent bookstore chain founded in Rossdale in 1986, announced today that it will celebrate its fortieth anniversary by opening stores in Kelmore, Branton Hills, and Verity Springs next year, the company's first new locations in over a decade.

Each new store will follow the format Pagewell introduced when it remodeled its flagship Rossdale shop four years ago: a carefully selected inventory of about 20,000 titles, a café serving coffee from local roasters, and an events space hosting author readings, book clubs, and children's story hours. That remodeling, initially questioned by some observers, increased the flagship store's sales by 31 percent in two years and is widely credited with reviving the company's fortunes.

"People predicted the end of physical bookstores for years, but our customers keep proving otherwise," said Pagewell president Nora Castellan, granddaughter of founder Arthur Pagewell. "What readers want is a place that feels personal. You cannot download a conversation about a novel you loved."

The company will hire about 25 employees for each location, with store managers recruited internally from existing branches. Hiring for the remaining positions will begin in January through the careers page of the Pagewell website. The Kelmore store is scheduled to open in May, followed by Branton Hills in August and Verity Springs in November.
